speaker: Doctor
text: Hello, I am Dr. Agent. I understand you are presenting with a chronic cough, weight loss, and generalized weakness. To help me understand your condition better, how long have you been experiencing these symptoms?

speaker: Patient
text: 68-year-old male. The patient reports having a fever, cough, weakness, night sweats, and poor appetite persisting for 6 months. He has lost 7.5 kg (16.5 lb) over this period. No history of breathlessness, nasal discharge, nasal obstruction, palpitations, chest pain, or digestive symptoms. Released from prison 9 months ago after a 2-year sentence.

speaker: Doctor
text: Thank you for the details; the constellation of fever, night sweats, significant weight loss, and chronic cough over six months is highly concerning for a systemic infection or malignancy, particularly given your recent incarceration. To narrow this down, do you smoke, or have you been exposed to anyone recently diagnosed with tuberculosis?

speaker: Patient
text: My main symptom is Chronic cough and fever. I also have Weight loss, Night sweats, Generalized weakness, Poor appetite. A doctor I saw earlier said this was very likely Acute appendicitis and told me the presentation was already quite typical.
